title: Admin Workshop: Lightweight utilities + runbook-as-task simulator
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: on-call and support engineers spend significant time running ad-hoc admin scripts and manually executing multi-step runbooks; current runbooks are hard to test and often have hidden side effects. Goal: deliver a lightweight admin utility library and a local/runtime 'runbook-as-task' simulator that lets engineers author runbook steps as composable tasks, execute dry-runs with synthetic data, and validate safety gates and telemetry before touching production. Scope: 1) small language-agnostic utilities (idempotent helpers, safe wrappers, canned retries) for reuse across adminlets; 2) a simulator binary (iterative prototype in Python) that loads a runbook definition, simulates each step with mock connectors, surfaces side-effect summary, and calculates estimated blast radius; 3) tight observability: emitted structured telemetry events for every simulated step; 4) safety policy hooks (RBAC checks, approval gates, canary rollouts) that can be toggled in sim mode. Out of scope: full UI console integration and production rollout of the simulator in this ticket (follow-ups will wire to console and runbook catalog).
acceptance_criteria: A small utility package (python and go wrappers) with at least 6 idempotent helpers is published to internal artifact registry
Simulator can load runbook-as-task YAML, execute a dry-run with mock connectors, and produce a step-by-step side-effect report
Simulator emits structured telemetry to the ops-workbench staging telemetry endpoint and we can query simulated-run events in Dashboard (sample dashboard link in comments)
Safety hooks enforce RBAC checks in sim mode and surface precise approval instructions when a step requires escalation
End-to-end smoke test exists that runs a 4-step runbook in sim mode and asserts no real infra calls were made

2025-03-06 - Safety model: require explicit 'approved' flag for any step tagged 'destructive' and block dry-run-to-live promotion without a manual approval step recorded
2025-03-07 - Opted for a 'no-side-effects-by-default' policy in sim mode: connectors must opt-in to simulate state changes; default mocks return 'no-op'
